1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.

4. // Memory Region — Specifications
5. //
6. // A memory region is a contiguous, non-wrapping half-open byte interval of the
7. // address space, `[start, start + size)`, tagged with metadata
8. // (type / permissions / cache policy). `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` is the same
9. // interval additionally constrained so both endpoints are page-aligned, making
10. // it directly usable for frame/page booking. Both region types share the single
11. // `MemoryRegionView` abstraction (the truncated wrapper forwards `view()` to its
12. // inner region).
13. //
14. // Addresses are abstracted to `int` through the universal `spec_addr` projection
15. // (defined in `page.spec.rs`, `pub uninterp spec fn spec_addr<T: Address>`),
16. // exactly as `PageAligned<T>` does. Using `spec_addr` — rather than a
17. // `T: View<V = int>` bound on the `View` impl — is what lets the `View` (and the
18. // `@`-based accessor contracts) be stated for a bare `T: Address`: the
19. // address-family `View` impls are all `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated and the
20. // generic exec `impl<T: Address> ...` blocks carry no `View` bound, so a

28. use crate::hal::mem::spec_addr;

30. // Abstract value of a memory region: the geometry `(start, size)` (in bytes,
31. // as mathematical integers) plus the three metadata tags callers observe.
32. pub struct MemoryRegionView {
33.     /// First valid byte address of the region. Equals the `start` supplied at
34.     /// construction; for the truncated variant it is page-aligned. Also the
35.     /// `Ord` key for both region types.
36.     pub start: int,
37.     /// Length of the region in bytes. The interval is `[start, start + size)`.
38.     /// For the truncated variant it is a multiple of the page size.
39.     pub size: int,
40.     /// Classification of the region (Usable / Reserved / Mmio / Bad).
41.     pub typ: MemoryRegionType,
42.     /// Access permissions granted over the region.
43.     pub perm: AccessPermission,
44.     /// Optional MMIO caching policy; `None` for non-MMIO regions.
45.     pub cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>,

48. impl MemoryRegionView {
49.     /// Non-empty, non-wrapping interval lying within the address space. This is
50.     /// the geometry every constructed region guarantees and that caller
51.     /// arithmetic (`size - 1`, `start + size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`) relies
52.     /// on: `size >= 1` (`new` rejects `size == 0`) and the inclusive end
53.     /// `start + size - 1` never overflows the widest address representation.
54.     pub open spec fn wf_geometry(self) -> bool {
55.         &&& self.size >= 1
56.         &&& self.start >= 0
57.         &&& self.start + self.size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
58.     }
59. 
60.     /// Exclusive end of the half-open interval `[start, end)`.
61.     pub open spec fn spec_end(self) -> int {
62.         self.start + self.size
63.     }
64. 
65.     /// Inclusive last byte address (callers compute `start + size - 1`).
66.     pub open spec fn spec_last(self) -> int {
67.         self.start + self.size - 1
68.     }
69. 
70.     /// Whether `addr` lies in `[start, start + size)`.
71.     pub open spec fn contains(self, addr: int) -> bool {
72.         self.start <= addr < self.start + self.size
73.     }

76.     /// policy changes; geometry and the other tags are preserved (`..self`).
77.     pub open spec fn spec_set_cache_policy(self, policy: MmioCachePolicy) -> MemoryRegionView {
78.         MemoryRegionView { cache_policy: Some(policy), ..self }
79.     }
80. }
81. 
82. // `MemoryRegion<T>` abstracts to its geometry plus tags. The `view()` is
83. // `closed`: callers reference `self@.start` / `self@.size` but the field-to-
84. // storage mapping (and the `spec_addr` projection of the typed `start`) does not
85. // leak. Unconditional over `T: Address` (see module comment).
86. impl<T: Address> View for MemoryRegion<T> {
87.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
88. 
89.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
90.         MemoryRegionView {
91.             start: spec_addr(&self.start),
92.             size: self.size as int,
93.             typ: self.typ,
94.             perm: self.perm,
95.             cache_policy: self.cache_policy,
96.         }
97.     }
98. }

100. // `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` is the same interval with a stronger invariant; its
101. // `view()` forwards to the inner `MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>`.
102. impl<T: Address> View for TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
103.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
104. 
105.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
106.         self.0@
107.     }
108. }
109. 
110. // Well-formedness of a base memory region: non-empty, non-wrapping geometry.
111. impl<T: Address> MemoryRegion<T> {
112.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
113.         self@.wf_geometry()
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. // Well-formedness of a truncated region: base geometry plus page alignment of
118. // both endpoints (established by `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`'s `align_up`), so
119. // `size / FRAME_SIZE` is exact and `start` needs no re-alignment.
120. impl<T: Address> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
121.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
122.         &&& self@.wf_geometry()
123.         &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0
124.         &&& self@.size % spec_page_size() == 0
125.     }
126. }

145. pub struct MemoryRegion<T: Address> {

147.     start: T,
148.     size: usize,
149.     typ: MemoryRegionType,
150.     perm: AccessPermission,
151.     cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>,
152. }

154. impl<T: Address> MemoryRegion<T> {
155.     /// Maximum byte-length of a memory region name.
156.     const MEMORY_REGION_NAME_MAX: usize = 32;
157. 
158.     /// Creates a new memory region.
159.     pub fn new(
160.         name: &str,
161.         start: T,
162.         size: usize,
163.         typ: MemoryRegionType,
164.         perm: AccessPermission,
165.     ) -> Result<Self, Error> {
166.         // Check if name is too long (byte length).
167.         if name.len() > Self::MEMORY_REGION_NAME_MAX {
168.             let reason: &str = "memory region name is too long";
169.             error!("{reason} (name.len={}, NAME_MAX={})", name.len(), Self::MEMORY_REGION_NAME_MAX);
170.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
171.         }
172. 
173.         // Check if size of the memory region is valid.
174.         if size == 0 {
175.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, "invalid memory region size"));
176.         }
177. 
178.         // Check if memory region is too big.
179.         let start_raw_addr: usize = start.clone().into_raw_value();
180.         let end_raw_addr: usize = match start_raw_addr.checked_add(size - 1) {
181.             Some(end_raw_addr) => end_raw_addr,
182.             None => {
183.                 return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::TooBig, "memory region is too big"));
184.             },
185.         };
186. 
187.         // Check if memory region spans outside the address space.
188.         if end_raw_addr > T::max_addr() {
189.             return Err(Error::new(
190.                 ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
191.                 "memory region spans outside the address space",
192.             ));
193.         }
194. 
195.         Ok(Self {
196.             name: name.to_string(),
197.             start,
198.             size,
199.             typ,
200.             perm,
201.             cache_policy: None,
202.         })
203.     }
204. 
205.     pub fn name(&self) -> String {
206.         self.name.clone()
207.     }
208. 
209.     /// Returns the first valid address that lies in the target memory region.
210.     #[verus_spec(result =>
211.         ensures
212.             // Faithful read: the returned address has the same abstract address
213.             // as the stored `start` (`spec_addr(&result) == self@.start`). `T` is
214.             // a bare `Address` (no `View` bound), so the value is projected
215.             // through the universal `spec_addr`, not `result@`. `Address: Copy`,
216.             // so the field read is identity (`result == self.start`), which
217.             // discharges the postcondition by congruence of `spec_addr`.
218.             crate::hal::mem::spec_addr(&result) == self@.start,
219.     )]

222.         // Verus limitation: `Clone::clone` on a generic `T: Address` has no spec
223.         // relating `spec_addr(&result)` to `spec_addr(&self.start)`, so the
224.         // postcondition `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` cannot be discharged

309. //==================================================================================================

311. ///
312. /// # Description
313. ///
314. /// A memory region that has been truncated to a multiple of a page size.
315. ///
316. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
317. #[derive(Clone)]
318. pub struct TruncatedMemoryRegion<T: Address>(MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>);

320. impl<T: Address> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
321.     /// Creates a new truncated memory region.
322.     pub fn new(
323.         name: &str,
324.         start: PageAligned<T>,
325.         size: usize,
326.         typ: MemoryRegionType,
327.         perm: AccessPermission,
328.     ) -> Result<Self, Error> {
329.         // Truncate the size of the memory region to a multiple of the page size.
330.         let size: usize = ::sys::mm::align_up(size, PAGE_ALIGNMENT).ok_or_else(|| {

338.     ///
339.     /// # Description
340.     ///
341.     /// Creates a new truncated MMIO memory region with an explicit cache policy.
342.     ///
343.     /// # Parameters
344.     ///
345.     /// - `name`: Name of the memory region.

347.     /// - `size`: Size of the region in bytes (rounded up to page alignment).

349.     /// - `cache_policy`: Caching policy that controls PWT/PCD bits in page table entries.
350.     ///
351.     /// # Returns
352.     ///
353.     /// Upon successful completion, a new [`TruncatedMemoryRegion`] with type
354.     /// [`MemoryRegionType::Mmio`] is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
355.     ///
356.     pub fn new_mmio(
357.         name: &str,
358.         start: PageAligned<T>,
359.         size: usize,
360.         perm: AccessPermission,
361.         cache_policy: MmioCachePolicy,
362.     ) -> Result<Self, Error> {
363.         let mut region: Self = Self::new(name, start, size, MemoryRegionType::Mmio, perm)?;
364.         region.0.set_cache_policy(cache_policy);
365.         Ok(region)
366.     }
367. 
368.     pub fn from_memory_region(region: MemoryRegion<T>) -> Result<Self, Error> {
369.         let cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy> = region.cache_policy();
370.         let start: T = region.start().align_down(PAGE_ALIGNMENT)?;
371.         let start: PageAligned<T> = PageAligned::from_address(start)?;
372.         let name: String = region.name();
373.         let size: usize = region.size();
374.         let typ: MemoryRegionType = region.typ();
375.         let perm: AccessPermission = region.perm();
376.         let mut truncated: Self = Self::new(&name, start, size, typ, perm)?;
377.         if let Some(policy) = cache_policy {
378.             truncated.0.set_cache_policy(policy);
379.         }
380.         Ok(truncated)
381.     }

384.         self.0.name()
385.     }

390.             // Faithful read, delegated to the inner region. The returned

394.             crate::hal::mem::spec_addr(&result) == self@.start,
395.     )]

397.         self.0.start()
398.     }

401.     #[verus_spec(result =>
402.         ensures
403.             result as int == self@.size,
404.     )]
405.     pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
406.         self.0.size()
407.     }
408.

410.     pub fn typ(&self) -> MemoryRegionType {
411.         self.0.typ()
412.     }
413. 
414.     /// Returns the permissions of the target memory region.
415.     pub fn perm(&self) -> AccessPermission {
416.         self.0.perm()
417.     }
418.

420.     /// # Description
421.     ///
422.     /// Returns the MMIO cache policy of the target memory region, if set.
423.     ///
424.     /// # Returns
425.     ///
426.     /// The [`MmioCachePolicy`] if one was assigned, or `None` otherwise.
427.     ///
428.     pub fn cache_policy(&self) -> Option<MmioCachePolicy> {
429.         self.0.cache_policy()
430.     }
431. }

434.     fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
435.         self.0 == other.0
436.     }
437. }

440.

442.     fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<core::cmp::Ordering> {
443.         Some(self.cmp(other))
444.     }

448.     fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> core::cmp::Ordering {

   (declared in `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.spec.rs`).
   `ensures result as int == addr@`.

   `external_type_specification` wrapper registering the foreign `arch::FrameNumber`
   as opaque. No body verified; carries no abstract guarantee beyond opacity.

 - `<VirtualAddress as Address>::into_raw_value` — `result as int == addr@`.

1. # View Design: hal::mem::types::region
2. 
3. Status: **review & refinement** of the View already present in the in-file
4. `verus! { }` block of `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/region.rs`. The existing
5. `MemoryRegionView` is sound and caller-abstract; this document confirms each
6. field against the substitution test, proposes a strengthened `inv()`, and
7. records the spec transition and reusable spec helpers that later phases will
8. reference.
9. 
10. In-scope verification-order targets:
11. `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start`, `MemoryRegion::start`,
12. `TruncatedMemoryRegion::size`, `MemoryRegion::size`. The View, however, is
13. module-level: it is the shared abstraction for *both* region types and all of
14. their accessors, not just the four targets.
15. 
16. ---
17. 
18. ## Abstract Resource
19. 
20. A **memory region** is a contiguous, non-wrapping half-open byte interval of the
21. address space, `[start, start + size)`, tagged with metadata
22. (type / permissions / cache policy). `TruncatedMemoryRegion` is the same
23. interval additionally constrained so both endpoints are page-aligned (`start`
24. page-aligned, `size` a multiple of the page size), making it directly usable for
25. frame/page booking.
26. 
27. From the caller's perspective the only state that matters is the **geometry**
28. `(start, size)` plus the three **metadata tags** that other accessors expose.
29. Everything else (the human-readable `name`, the wrapping of one struct inside
30. another for the truncated variant, the physical layout of the fields) is
31. internal.
32. 
33. ---
34. 
35. ## View Struct
36. 
37. Both `MemoryRegion<T>` and `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` map to the **same** View
38. type. The truncated wrapper forwards `view()` to its inner region, so a single
39. abstraction describes both. `T: Address + View<V = int>`, hence addresses are
40. abstracted to `int`.
41. 
42. ```rust
43. pub struct MemoryRegionView {
44.     /// First valid byte address of the region (abstract address, in bytes).
45.     /// Equals the `start` supplied at construction; for the truncated variant
46.     /// it is page-aligned. This is also the Ord key for both region types.
47.     pub start: int,
48.     /// Length of the region in bytes. The interval is [start, start + size).
49.     /// For the truncated variant it is a multiple of the page size.
50.     pub size: int,
51.     /// Classification of the region (Usable / Reserved / Mmio / Bad).
52.     pub typ: MemoryRegionType,
53.     /// Access permissions granted over the region.
54.     pub perm: AccessPermission,
55.     /// Optional MMIO caching policy (PWT/PCD); `None` for non-MMIO regions.
56.     pub cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>,
57. }
58. ```
59. 
60. `view()` stays `closed` on both impls (callers reference `self@.start` etc. but
61. the field-to-storage mapping does not leak). The impls are **unconditional**
62. over `T: Address` and project the typed `start` through the universal
63. `spec_addr<T: Address>` ghost function (defined in `page.spec.rs`), exactly as
64. `PageAligned<T>` does — **not** via a `T: View<V = int>` bound and `self.start@`:
65. 
66. ```rust
67. impl<T: Address> View for MemoryRegion<T> {
68.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
69.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
70.         MemoryRegionView { start: spec_addr(&self.start), size: self.size as int, .. }
71.     }
72. }
73. 
74. impl<T: Address> View for TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
75.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
76.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView { self.0@ }   // forward
77. }
78. ```
79. 
80. > **Design change (implemented).** The originally-proposed
81. > `impl<T: Address + View<V = int>>` bound is **not usable**: the in-scope exec
82. > accessors live in `impl<T: Address> ...` blocks (no `View` bound), so a
83. > conditional `View` impl makes `self@` untypable inside them
84. > (`error[E0599]: MemoryRegion<T>: View not satisfied`). Moreover the
85. > address-family `View` impls are all `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated, so a
86. > `T: View<V = int>` bound would be unsatisfiable in a normal `cargo build`.
87. > The fix mirrors the established `PageAligned<T>` pattern: make `View`
88. > unconditional and project addresses through the universal `spec_addr`. This
89. > keeps the `view()` closed and the abstraction `T`-agnostic while letting every
90. > accessor contract typecheck for a bare `T: Address`.
91. 
92. ---
93. 
94. ## Well-formedness Invariant
95. 
96. The current in-file `inv()` (defined only on `TruncatedMemoryRegion`) captures
97. **only** page alignment:
98. 
99. ```rust
100. &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0
101. &&& self@.size  % spec_page_size() == 0
102. ```
103. 
104. The caller analysis shows two further geometry properties that every constructed
105. region guarantees and that callers *depend on* for their arithmetic
106. (`size - 1`, `start + size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`). These should be made part
107. of the abstract well-formedness so they are available wherever a region is in
108. scope. Recommended layering:
109. 
110. ```rust
111. // Shared geometry well-formedness, valid for BOTH region types.
112. // (Proposed as a reusable helper on the View — see "Spec Helpers" below.)
113. //   non-empty:  size >= 1                (new rejects size == 0)
114. //   no-wrap:    start >= 0 && start + size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
115. //               (the interval fits the address space; start + size - 1 never
116. //                overflows, so inclusive-end / frame-range math is well-defined)
117. 
118. impl<T: Address + View<V = int>> MemoryRegion<T> {
119.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
120.         self@.wf_geometry()
121.     }
122. }
123. 
124. impl<T: Address + View<V = int>> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
125.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
126.         &&& self@.wf_geometry()                       // size >= 1, no wrap
127.         &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0       // page-aligned start
128.         &&& self@.size  % spec_page_size() == 0       // page-multiple size
129.     }
130. }
131. ```
132. 
133. Notes:
134. - The no-wrap bound is stated abstractly against `usize::MAX` (the widest
135.   address representation). The concrete `T::max_addr()` bound enforced by `new`
136.   is *stronger*; the View only needs the weaker no-wrap fact because that is all
137.   caller arithmetic relies on, and it keeps the invariant `T`-agnostic.
138. - **Implemented as designed.** Both `MemoryRegion::inv` (`wf_geometry()`) and the
139.   strengthened `TruncatedMemoryRegion::inv` (`wf_geometry()` + page alignment) are
140.   in `region.spec.rs`. Adding `wf_geometry` caused no proof churn: `inv()` is an
141.   `open spec fn` referenced by no in-scope contract, so it imposes no obligation
142.   on the four accessors (it documents the abstract well-formedness for callers
143.   and future phases). `wf_geometry`, `spec_end`, `spec_last`, `contains`, and the
144.   `spec_set_cache_policy` transition are all present as View helpers.
145. 
146. ---
147. 
148. ## Spec Helpers (on the View type)
149. 
150. Per the skill, reusable spec logic lives on the View, not as extra `pub spec
151. fn`s on the region impls. These encode exactly the derived quantities callers
152. compute, so later `ensures` can hand them back directly.
153. 
154. ```rust
155. impl MemoryRegionView {
156.     /// Non-empty, non-wrapping interval within the address space.
157.     pub open spec fn wf_geometry(self) -> bool {
158.         &&& self.size >= 1
159.         &&& self.start >= 0
160.         &&& self.start + self.size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
161.     }
162. 
163.     /// Exclusive end of the half-open interval [start, end).
164.     pub open spec fn spec_end(self) -> int { self.start + self.size }
165. 
166.     /// Inclusive last byte address (callers compute `start + size - 1`).
167.     pub open spec fn spec_last(self) -> int { self.start + self.size - 1 }
168. 
169.     /// Whether `addr` lies in [start, start + size).
170.     pub open spec fn contains(self, addr: int) -> bool {
171.         self.start <= addr < self.start + self.size
172.     }
173. }
174. ```
175. 
176. These are optional conveniences for downstream phases; the four target
177. accessors themselves only need `result@ == self@.start` / `result == self@.size`
178. style `ensures`. They are listed so spec authors reuse one definition of
179. "inclusive end" / "contains" instead of re-deriving overflow-prone arithmetic.
180. 
181. ---
182. 
183. ## Spec Transition Functions
184. 
185. The region types are almost entirely immutable. The **only** state-mutating
186. exec function in the module is `MemoryRegion::set_cache_policy`, so it gets the
187. sole transition (it is out of the current four-function scope but belongs to the
188. View design for completeness):
189. 
190. ```rust
191. impl MemoryRegionView {
192.     pub open spec fn spec_set_cache_policy(self, policy: MmioCachePolicy) -> MemoryRegionView {
193.         MemoryRegionView { cache_policy: Some(policy), ..self }   // frame: geometry + tags preserved
194.     }
195. }
196. // ensures self@ == old(self)@.spec_set_cache_policy(policy)
197. ```
198. 
199. `..self` is the frame condition: `start`, `size`, `typ`, `perm` are unchanged.
200. 
201. The constructors (`MemoryRegion::new`, `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`,
202. `new_mmio`, `from_memory_region`, `from_virtual_memory_region`) are *creation*,
203. not `self`-transitions; they will be specified in later phases by stating the
204. resulting `self@` (e.g. `result@.start == start@`, `result@.size` rounded up to
205. a page multiple for the truncated path) rather than via a transition on an
206. existing View. No transition function is owed for them here.
207. 
208. The four in-scope accessors are pure reads — no transition, just `ensures`
209. linking the return value to the View field. Because the return types (`T`,
210. `PageAligned<T>`) are bare `Address` values (no `View` bound in the exec impl),
211. the returned address is projected through `spec_addr`, not `result@`:
212. 
213. | Function | Implemented ensures |
214. |----------|----------------------------|
215. | `MemoryRegion::start`            | `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` |
216. | `MemoryRegion::size`             | `result as int == self@.size`   |
217. | `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start`   | `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` (page alignment of `self@.start` follows from `self.inv()`) |
218. | `TruncatedMemoryRegion::size`    | `result as int == self@.size`   |
219. 
220. `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start` delegates to `MemoryRegion::start`; the forwarding
221. `view()` (`self@ == self.0@`) makes `spec_addr(&result) == self.0@.start ==
222. self@.start` discharge by delegation. `MemoryRegion::start` itself carries a
223. specification-phase `admit()` placeholder: relating `spec_addr(&self.start.clone())`
224. to `spec_addr(&self.start)` needs a value-preserving clone spec on the `Address`
225. family, which is supplied in the proving phase.
226. 
227. ---
228. 
229. ## Design Rationale (per field, substitution test)
230. 
231. > Substitution test: *if the implementation were completely rewritten with a
232. > different algorithm, would this field still make sense?*
233. 
234. | Field | Caller-observable via | Substitution test | Verdict |
235. |-------|-----------------------|--------------------|---------|
236. | `start: int` | `start()` (10 ext. sites: frame number, raw value, identity-map base, overlap key, Ord key) | Any region representation must expose a first address; callers read it as a frame/page base and as the ordering key. Independent of how it is stored (`T` vs `PageAligned<T>`). | ✅ keep |
237. | `size: int` | `size()` (8 ext. sites: `size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`, region end, identity-map end) | Any representation must expose a byte length; callers do exact frame division and inclusive-end math. Survives any storage/truncation strategy. | ✅ keep |
238. | `typ: MemoryRegionType` | `typ()` (14 refs) — routing/classification of regions | The classification is intrinsic region state, not an implementation artifact; survives a rewrite. Needed so `typ()` can later be specified. | ✅ keep |
239. | `perm: AccessPermission` | `perm()` — permissions consumed when mapping | Intrinsic region attribute, independent of layout. | ✅ keep |
240. | `cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>` | `cache_policy()` / mutated by `set_cache_policy()` | Intrinsic MMIO attribute and the target of the module's only mutator; the transition spec needs it. | ✅ keep |
241. 
242. Abstract-type choices: `int` for `start`/`size` (not `usize`/`T`) so spec
243. arithmetic — inclusive end, frame ranges, overlap — is overflow-free and matches
244. how every caller uses the values (`into_raw_value()` then integer math). `Option`
245. mirrors the optional cache policy. `typ`/`perm` are small `Copy` enums/structs
246. carried as-is; abstracting them further would add no caller value.
247. 
248. Shared View for both region types: the truncated variant *is* the same interval
249. with a stronger invariant, and its `view()` forwards to the inner region. One
250. View + a stronger `inv()` is simpler than two near-identical View types and lets
251. callers (e.g. `MmioRegion::base`/`size`, the mmio allocator) reason uniformly.
252. 
253. `view()` closed / `inv()` open: `closed` hides the field→storage mapping (e.g.
254. that truncated regions wrap `MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>`); `open` `inv()`
255. exposes the page-alignment and geometry facts callers must rely on
256. (`size / FRAME_SIZE` exact, `start` needs no re-alignment).
257. 
258. ---
259. 
260. ## Rejected Alternatives
261. 
262. - **`name: String` field** — `name()` is a public accessor, but the caller
263.   analysis explicitly states callers "don't care about" the name for any
264.   geometry/booking use, and no in-scope spec references it. Including it fails
265.   *minimality* (no spec uses it) without aiding any caller. It is display /
266.   identity metadata; if `name()` is ever brought into scope, add a
267.   `name: Seq<char>` field then. **Excluded.**
268. 
269. - **`start: T` / `start: PageAligned<T>` (machine/typed address)** — mirrors the
270.   implementation field and forces callers to unwrap before doing arithmetic.
271.   Fails the abstract-type rule. The `int` abstraction (via `T::view() == int`)
272.   is what every caller actually computes on. **Excluded.**
273. 
274. - **`size: usize` / `nat`** — `usize` re-introduces overflow into specs;
275.   `nat` would block expressing the no-wrap bound against `usize::MAX as int`
276.   cleanly and complicates `size - 1` reasoning. `int` is the right spec type.
277.   **Excluded.**
278. 
279. - **`end: int` as a stored field (instead of `size`)** — redundant with
280.   `start + size`; storing both invites an extra consistency clause in `inv()`.
281.   Callers want *both* numbers, but only one is primitive state — `end` is a
282.   derived helper (`spec_end`), not a field. **Excluded as a field; kept as a
283.   helper.**
284. 
285. - **A separate `TruncatedMemoryRegionView`** — would duplicate all five fields
286.   to add nothing but the page-alignment facts, which belong in `inv()` not in a
287.   new struct. The `closed` forwarding `view()` already gives the truncated type
288.   its own abstraction surface. **Excluded.**
289. 
290. - **`is_truncated: bool` / a tag distinguishing the two region kinds** — the
291.   Rust type already distinguishes them; encoding it in the shared View would be
292.   a type-system fact restated as spec state (an anti-pattern) and unused by any
293.   caller. **Excluded.**
294. 
295. - **`internal_inv()` mirroring private fields** — there is no internal
296.   bookkeeping beyond the five abstract fields; the only "hidden" structure is
297.   the wrapper nesting, which is a `closed view()` concern, not an invariant.
298.   No separate internal invariant is warranted. **Excluded.**
299. 
300. ---
301. 
302. ## Quality Review
303. 
304. | Criterion | Check |
305. |-----------|-------|
306. | **Substitution** | All five fields describe intrinsic region state surviving any rewrite. ✅ |
307. | **Caller-only** | Every field is exposed by a public accessor and used by real callers (geometry by the four targets; tags by `typ`/`perm`/`cache_policy`). ✅ |
308. | **Complete** | `(start, size)` + tags cover every caller-observable concept in the analysis (frame math, overlap, Ord key, routing, MMIO policy). ✅ |
309. | **Minimal** | No unused field — `name` deliberately omitted. Each field maps to ≥1 (current or near-term) spec. ✅ |
310. | **No code-as-spec** | View states *what* a region is (an interval + tags), not *how* it is stored or truncated. ✅ |
311.

 > keeps the `view()` closed and the abstraction `T`-agnostic while letting every
 > accessor contract typecheck for a bare `T: Address`.
 
 ---
 
 ## Well-formedness Invariant
 
 The current in-file `inv()` (defined only on `TruncatedMemoryRegion`) captures
 **only** page alignment:
 
 ```rust
 &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0
 &&& self@.size  % spec_page_size() == 0
 ```
 
 The caller analysis shows two further geometry properties that every constructed
 region guarantees and that callers *depend on* for their arithmetic
 (`size - 1`, `start + size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`). These should be made part
 of the abstract well-formedness so they are available wherever a region is in
 scope. Recommended layering:
 
 ```rust
 // Shared geometry well-formedness, valid for BOTH region types.
 // (Proposed as a reusable helper on the View — see "Spec Helpers" below.)
 //   non-empty:  size >= 1                (new rejects size == 0)
 //   no-wrap:    start >= 0 && start + size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
 //               (the interval fits the address space; start + size - 1 never
 //                overflows, so inclusive-end / frame-range math is well-defined)
 
 impl<T: Address + View<V = int>> MemoryRegion<T> {
     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
         self@.wf_geometry()
     }
 }
 
 impl<T: Address + View<V = int>> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
         &&& self@.wf_geometry()                       // size >= 1, no wrap
         &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0       // page-aligned start
         &&& self@.size  % spec_page_size() == 0       // page-multiple size
     }
 }
 ```
 
 Notes:
 - The no-wrap bound is stated abstractly against `usize::MAX` (the widest
   address representation). The concrete `T::max_addr()` bound enforced by `new`
   is *stronger*; the View only needs the weaker no-wrap fact because that is all
   caller arithmetic relies on, and it keeps the invariant `T`-agnostic.
 - **Implemented as designed.** Both `MemoryRegion::inv` (`wf_geometry()`) and the
   strengthened `TruncatedMemoryRegion::inv` (`wf_geometry()` + page alignment) are
   in `region.spec.rs`. Adding `wf_geometry` caused no proof churn: `inv()` is an
   `open spec fn` referenced by no in-scope contract, so it imposes no obligation
   on the four accessors (it documents the abstract well-formedness for callers
   and future phases). `wf_geometry`, `spec_end`, `spec_last`, `contains`, and the
   `spec_set_cache_policy` transition are all present as View helpers.
 
 ---
 
 ## Spec Helpers (on the View type)
 
 Per the skill, reusable spec logic lives on the View, not as extra `pub spec
 fn`s on the region impls. These encode exactly the derived quantities callers
 compute, so later `ensures` can hand them back directly.
 
 ```rust
 impl MemoryRegionView {
     /// Non-empty, non-wrapping interval within the address space.
     pub open spec fn wf_geometry(self) -> bool {
         &&& self.size >= 1
         &&& self.start >= 0
         &&& self.start + self.size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
     }
 
     /// Exclusive end of the half-open interval [start, end).
     pub open spec fn spec_end(self) -> int { self.start + self.size }
 
     /// Inclusive last byte address (callers compute `start + size - 1`).
     pub open spec fn spec_last(self) -> int { self.start + self.size - 1 }
 
     /// Whether `addr` lies in [start, start + size).
     pub open spec fn contains(self, addr: int) -> bool {
         self.start <= addr < self.start + self.size
     }
 }
 ```
 
 These are optional conveniences for downstream phases; the four target
 accessors themselves only need `result@ == self@.start` / `result == self@.size`
 style `ensures`. They are listed so spec authors reuse one definition of
 "inclusive end" / "contains" instead of re-deriving overflow-prone arithmetic.
 
 ---
 
 ## Spec Transition Functions
 
 The region types are almost entirely immutable. The **only** state-mutating
 exec function in the module is `MemoryRegion::set_cache_policy`, so it gets the
 sole transition (it is out of the current four-function scope but belongs to the
 View design for completeness):
 
 ```rust
 impl MemoryRegionView {
     pub open spec fn spec_set_cache_policy(self, policy: MmioCachePolicy) -> MemoryRegionView {
         MemoryRegionView { cache_policy: Some(policy), ..self }   // frame: geometry + tags preserved
     }
 }
 // ensures self@ == old(self)@.spec_set_cache_policy(policy)
 ```
 
 `..self` is the frame condition: `start`, `size`, `typ`, `perm` are unchanged.
 
 The constructors (`MemoryRegion::new`, `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`,
 `new_mmio`, `from_memory_region`, `from_virtual_memory_region`) are *creation*,
 not `self`-transitions; they will be specified in later phases by stating the
 resulting `self@` (e.g. `result@.start == start@`, `result@.size` rounded up to
 a page multiple for the truncated path) rather than via a transition on an
 existing View. No transition function is owed for them here.
 
 The four in-scope accessors are pure reads — no transition, just `ensures`
 linking the return value to the View field. Because the return types (`T`,
 `PageAligned<T>`) are bare `Address` values (no `View` bound in the exec impl),
 the returned address is projected through `spec_addr`, not `result@`:
 
 | Function | Implemented ensures |
 |----------|----------------------------|
 | `MemoryRegion::start`            | `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` |
 | `MemoryRegion::size`             | `result as int == self@.size`   |
 | `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start`   | `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` (page alignment of `self@.start` follows from `self.inv()`) |
 | `TruncatedMemoryRegion::size`    | `result as int == self@.size`   |
 
 `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start` delegates to `MemoryRegion::start`; the forwarding
 `view()` (`self@ == self.0@`) makes `spec_addr(&result) == self.0@.start ==
 self@.start` discharge by delegation. `MemoryRegion::start` itself carries a
 specification-phase `admit()` placeholder: relating `spec_addr(&self.start.clone())`
 to `spec_addr(&self.start)` needs a value-preserving clone spec on the `Address`
 family, which is supplied in the proving phase.
 
 ---
 
 ## Design Rationale (per field, substitution test)
 
 > Substitution test: *if the implementation were completely rewritten with a
 > different algorithm, would this field still make sense?*
 
 | Field | Caller-observable via | Substitution test | Verdict |
 |-------|-----------------------|--------------------|---------|
 | `start: int` | `start()` (10 ext. sites: frame number, raw value, identity-map base, overlap key, Ord key) | Any region representation must expose a first address; callers read it as a frame/page base and as the ordering key. Independent of how it is stored (`T` vs `PageAligned<T>`). | ✅ keep |
 | `size: int` | `size()` (8 ext. sites: `size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`, region end, identity-map end) | Any representation must expose a byte length; callers do exact frame division and inclusive-end math. Survives any storage/truncation strategy. | ✅ keep |
 | `typ: MemoryRegionType` | `typ()` (14 refs) — routing/classification of regions | The classification is intrinsic region state, not an implementation artifact; survives a rewrite. Needed so `typ()` can later be specified. | ✅ keep |
 | `perm: AccessPermission` | `perm()` — permissions consumed when mapping | Intrinsic region attribute, independent of layout. | ✅ keep |
 | `cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>` | `cache_policy()` / mutated by `set_cache_policy()` | Intrinsic MMIO attribute and the target of the module's only mutator; the transition spec needs it. | ✅ keep |
 
 Abstract-type choices: `int` for `start`/`size` (not `usize`/`T`) so spec
 arithmetic — inclusive end, frame ranges, overlap — is overflow-free and matches
 how every caller uses the values (`into_raw_value()` then integer math). `Option`
 mirrors the optional cache policy. `typ`/`perm` are small `Copy` enums/structs
 carried as-is; abstracting them further would add no caller value.
 
 Shared View for both region types: the truncated variant *is* the same interval
 with a stronger invariant, and its `view()` forwards to the inner region. One
 View + a stronger `inv()` is simpler than two near-identical View types and lets
 callers (e.g. `MmioRegion::base`/`size`, the mmio allocator) reason uniformly.
 
 `view()` closed / `inv()` open: `closed` hides the field→storage mapping (e.g.
 that truncated regions wrap `MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>`); `open` `inv()`
 exposes the page-alignment and geometry facts callers must rely on
 (`size / FRAME_SIZE` exact, `start` needs no re-alignment).
 
 ---
 
 ## Rejected Alternatives
 
 - **`name: String` field** — `name()` is a public accessor, but the caller
   analysis explicitly states callers "don't care about" the name for any
   geometry/booking use, and no in-scope spec references it. Including it fails
   *minimality* (no spec uses it) without aiding any caller. It is display /
   identity metadata; if `name()` is ever brought into scope, add a
   `name: Seq<char>` field then. **Excluded.**
 
 - **`start: T` / `start: PageAligned<T>` (machine/typed address)** — mirrors the
   implementation field and forces callers to unwrap before doing arithmetic.
   Fails the abstract-type rule. The `int` abstraction (via `T::view() == int`)
   is what every caller actually computes on. **Excluded.**
 
 - **`size: usize` / `nat`** — `usize` re-introduces overflow into specs;
   `nat` would block expressing the no-wrap bound against `usize::MAX as int`
   cleanly and complicates `size - 1` reasoning. `int` is the right spec type.
   **Excluded.**
 
 - **`end: int` as a stored field (instead of `size`)** — redundant with
   `start + size`; storing both invites an extra consistency clause in `inv()`.
   Callers want *both* numbers, but only one is primitive state — `end` is a
   derived helper (`spec_end`), not a field. **Excluded as a field; kept as a
   helper.**
 
 - **A separate `TruncatedMemoryRegionView`** — would duplicate all five fields
   to add nothing but the page-alignment facts, which belong in `inv()` not in a
   new struct. The `closed` forwarding `view()` already gives the truncated type
   its own abstraction surface. **Excluded.**
 
 - **`is_truncated: bool` / a tag distinguishing the two region kinds** — the
   Rust type already distinguishes them; encoding it in the shared View would be
   a type-system fact restated as spec state (an anti-pattern) and unused by any
   caller. **Excluded.**
 
 - **`internal_inv()` mirroring private fields** — there is no internal
   bookkeeping beyond the five abstract fields; the only "hidden" structure is
   the wrapper nesting, which is a `closed view()` concern, not an invariant.
   No separate internal invariant is warranted. **Excluded.**
 
 ---
 
 ## Quality Review
 
 | Criterion | Check |
 |-----------|-------|
 | **Substitution** | All five fields describe intrinsic region state surviving any rewrite. ✅ |
 | **Caller-only** | Every field is exposed by a public accessor and used by real callers (geometry by the four targets; tags by `typ`/`perm`/`cache_policy`). ✅ |
 | **Complete** | `(start, size)` + tags cover every caller-observable concept in the analysis (frame math, overlap, Ord key, routing, MMIO policy). ✅ |
 | **Minimal** | No unused field — `name` deliberately omitted. Each field maps to ≥1 (current or near-term) spec. ✅ |
 | **No code-as-spec** | View states *what* a region is (an interval + tags), not *how* it is stored or truncated. ✅ |

---
name: ast-consistency
description: "AST-level exec fidelity checking tools and pre-approved deviations. Use after modifying source files to verify exec code is unchanged."
---

# AST Consistency Check

Source exec code must not change during verification — see `verus-constraints`
for the full rules. This skill covers the **tooling** to enforce that guarantee.

## Tools

The checker uses tree-sitter to hash exec code after stripping all
ghost/proof/spec annotations. It detects changes invisible to textual diff.

`scripts/ast_consistency.py` provides four subcommands:
- `count` — quick pass/fail
- `summary` — per-element status table
- `diff --name "Fn::name"` — unified diff for one function/struct
- `report -o <dir>` — full report with all diffs

The `source` argument is optional. Use `--base-ref` to extract the original
from git, or omit both on `verus-ai/*` branches for auto-detection:

```bash
# Explicit original file:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py original.rs verified.rs count

# Via git ref:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py --base-ref main verified.rs count

# Auto-detect on verus-ai/* branches:
python3 scripts/ast_consistency.py verified.rs count
```

`diff` with `--full` shows specs; default is exec-only.

**MCP alternative**: If the `verus-ast` MCP server is registered, the same
functionality is available as tools (`ast_count`, `ast_summary`, `ast_diff`,
`ast_report`) with the same auto-detection.

## Pre-Approved Deviations

These minimal exec changes are known Verus limitations — no full deviation
process needed, but still document with a comment:

| Original | Verus Version | Reason |
|----------|--------------|--------|
| `self.x += 1` | `self.x = self.x + 1` | Compound assignment unsupported |
| `self.arr[i] \|= v` | `self.arr.set(i, self.arr[i] \| v)` | Mutable index unsupported |
| `-> T` | `-> (ret: T)` | Named returns for ensures |
| `#[derive(Clone, ...)]` | `#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))] #[derive(...)]` | cfg-gating incompatible derives |
| `Ok(Self { .. })` | `let result = Self { .. }; Ok(result)` | Ensures needs to reference return value |
| `f(complex_expr)` | `let x = complex_expr; f(x)` | Intermediate value for assertions |
| `.ok_or_else(\|\| ...)` | `match ... { Some(v) => v, None => return Err(...) }` | Closures unsupported in some contexts |
| `v.std_method(args)` | `wrapper(&mut v, args)` | `&mut T` method unsupported; see `verus-constraints` skill for wrapper rules |

### Bug Fix Deviations

Exec changes that fix verified bugs are also pre-approved. These must:
- Have a `// VERUS BUG FIX: <description>` comment at the fix site
- Be recorded in `bugs.md` with full evidence
- Be committed with `[verus-ai] BUG FIX:` prefix
- Be limited to auto-fixable categories (overflow, off-by-one, missing
  bounds check, unchecked cast) — see `bug-reporting` skill

## Handling MISMATCHes

When the checker reports a MISMATCH:

1. **Default: restore original code.** Exec changes are violations. Use
   `git show <base_ref>:path/to/file.rs` to view the original, then
   manually restore the changed exec code while keeping your annotations.
   Adapt the proof to the original code — not the other way around.
2. **Check pre-approved deviations.** If the change matches one above,
   keep it but add a comment documenting which deviation and why.
3. **Verify it's a real Verus limitation.** Before accepting any other
   change, confirm Verus genuinely cannot handle the original construct:
   - Search vstd for existing support (e.g. `checked_mul` has vstd specs)
   - Try alternative proof strategies that preserve the original code
   - Build a minimal reproducer proving the limitation
4. **If confirmed, document with full evidence.** Add a `VERUS DEVIATION`
   comment explaining: what was changed, why the original doesn't work,
   what alternatives were tried, and why this is the smallest possible change.

4. // Memory Region — Specifications
5. //
6. // A memory region is a contiguous, non-wrapping half-open byte interval of the
7. // address space, `[start, start + size)`, tagged with metadata
8. // (type / permissions / cache policy). `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` is the same
9. // interval additionally constrained so both endpoints are page-aligned, making
10. // it directly usable for frame/page booking. Both region types share the single
11. // `MemoryRegionView` abstraction (the truncated wrapper forwards `view()` to its
12. // inner region).
13. //
14. // Addresses are abstracted to `int` through the universal `spec_addr` projection
15. // (defined in `page.spec.rs`, `pub uninterp spec fn spec_addr<T: Address>`),
16. // exactly as `PageAligned<T>` does. Using `spec_addr` — rather than a
17. // `T: View<V = int>` bound on the `View` impl — is what lets the `View` (and the
18. // `@`-based accessor contracts) be stated for a bare `T: Address`: the
19. // address-family `View` impls are all `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated and the
20. // generic exec `impl<T: Address> ...` blocks carry no `View` bound, so a
21. // conditional `View<V = int>` bound would make `self@` untypable inside the
22. // accessors. `spec_page_size()` is the canonical page size, re-exported from
23. // `crate::hal::mem`.
24. 
25. verus! {
26. 
27. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
28. use crate::hal::mem::spec_addr;
29. 
30. // Abstract value of a memory region: the geometry `(start, size)` (in bytes,
31. // as mathematical integers) plus the three metadata tags callers observe.
32. pub struct MemoryRegionView {
33.     /// First valid byte address of the region. Equals the `start` supplied at
34.     /// construction; for the truncated variant it is page-aligned. Also the
35.     /// `Ord` key for both region types.
36.     pub start: int,
37.     /// Length of the region in bytes. The interval is `[start, start + size)`.
38.     /// For the truncated variant it is a multiple of the page size.
39.     pub size: int,
40.     /// Classification of the region (Usable / Reserved / Mmio / Bad).
41.     pub typ: MemoryRegionType,
42.     /// Access permissions granted over the region.
43.     pub perm: AccessPermission,
44.     /// Optional MMIO caching policy; `None` for non-MMIO regions.
45.     pub cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>,
46. }
47. 
48. impl MemoryRegionView {
49.     /// Non-empty, non-wrapping interval lying within the address space. This is
50.     /// the geometry every constructed region guarantees and that caller
51.     /// arithmetic (`size - 1`, `start + size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`) relies
52.     /// on: `size >= 1` (`new` rejects `size == 0`) and the inclusive end
53.     /// `start + size - 1` never overflows the widest address representation.
54.     pub open spec fn wf_geometry(self) -> bool {
55.         &&& self.size >= 1
56.         &&& self.start >= 0
57.         &&& self.start + self.size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
58.     }
59. 
60.     /// Exclusive end of the half-open interval `[start, end)`.
61.     pub open spec fn spec_end(self) -> int {
62.         self.start + self.size
63.     }
64. 
65.     /// Inclusive last byte address (callers compute `start + size - 1`).
66.     pub open spec fn spec_last(self) -> int {
67.         self.start + self.size - 1
68.     }
69. 
70.     /// Whether `addr` lies in `[start, start + size)`.
71.     pub open spec fn contains(self, addr: int) -> bool {
72.         self.start <= addr < self.start + self.size
73.     }
74. 
75.     /// State transition of `MemoryRegion::set_cache_policy`: only the cache
76.     /// policy changes; geometry and the other tags are preserved (`..self`).
77.     pub open spec fn spec_set_cache_policy(self, policy: MmioCachePolicy) -> MemoryRegionView {
78.         MemoryRegionView { cache_policy: Some(policy), ..self }
79.     }
80. }
81. 
82. // `MemoryRegion<T>` abstracts to its geometry plus tags. The `view()` is
83. // `closed`: callers reference `self@.start` / `self@.size` but the field-to-
84. // storage mapping (and the `spec_addr` projection of the typed `start`) does not
85. // leak. Unconditional over `T: Address` (see module comment).
86. impl<T: Address> View for MemoryRegion<T> {
87.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
88. 
89.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
90.         MemoryRegionView {
91.             start: spec_addr(&self.start),
92.             size: self.size as int,
93.             typ: self.typ,
94.             perm: self.perm,
95.             cache_policy: self.cache_policy,
96.         }
97.     }
98. }
99. 
100. // `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` is the same interval with a stronger invariant; its
101. // `view()` forwards to the inner `MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>`.
102. impl<T: Address> View for TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
103.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
104. 
105.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
106.         self.0@
107.     }
108. }
109. 
110. // Well-formedness of a base memory region: non-empty, non-wrapping geometry.
111. impl<T: Address> MemoryRegion<T> {
112.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
113.         self@.wf_geometry()
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. // Well-formedness of a truncated region: base geometry plus page alignment of
118. // both endpoints (established by `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`'s `align_up`), so
119. // `size / FRAME_SIZE` is exact and `start` needs no re-alignment.
120. impl<T: Address> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
121.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
122.         &&& self@.wf_geometry()
123.         &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0
124.         &&& self@.size % spec_page_size() == 0
125.     }
126. }
127. 
128. } // verus!

141. /// A memory region.

143. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
144. #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
145. pub struct MemoryRegion<T: Address> {
146.     name: String,
147.     start: T,
148.     size: usize,
149.     typ: MemoryRegionType,
150.     perm: AccessPermission,
151.     cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>,
152. }
153. 
154. impl<T: Address> MemoryRegion<T> {
155.     /// Maximum byte-length of a memory region name.
156.     const MEMORY_REGION_NAME_MAX: usize = 32;
157. 
158.     /// Creates a new memory region.
159.     pub fn new(
160.         name: &str,
161.         start: T,
162.         size: usize,
163.         typ: MemoryRegionType,
164.         perm: AccessPermission,
165.     ) -> Result<Self, Error> {
166.         // Check if name is too long (byte length).
167.         if name.len() > Self::MEMORY_REGION_NAME_MAX {
168.             let reason: &str = "memory region name is too long";
169.             error!("{reason} (name.len={}, NAME_MAX={})", name.len(), Self::MEMORY_REGION_NAME_MAX);
170.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
171.         }
172. 
173.         // Check if size of the memory region is valid.
174.         if size == 0 {
175.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, "invalid memory region size"));
176.         }
177. 
178.         // Check if memory region is too big.
179.         let start_raw_addr: usize = start.clone().into_raw_value();
180.         let end_raw_addr: usize = match start_raw_addr.checked_add(size - 1) {
181.             Some(end_raw_addr) => end_raw_addr,
182.             None => {
183.                 return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::TooBig, "memory region is too big"));
184.             },
185.         };
186. 
187.         // Check if memory region spans outside the address space.
188.         if end_raw_addr > T::max_addr() {
189.             return Err(Error::new(
190.                 ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
191.                 "memory region spans outside the address space",
192.             ));
193.         }
194. 
195.         Ok(Self {
196.             name: name.to_string(),
197.             start,
198.             size,
199.             typ,
200.             perm,
201.             cache_policy: None,
202.         })
203.     }
204. 
205.     pub fn name(&self) -> String {
206.         self.name.clone()
207.     }
208. 
209.     /// Returns the first valid address that lies in the target memory region.
210.     #[verus_spec(result =>
211.         ensures
212.             // Faithful read: the returned address has the same abstract address
213.             // as the stored `start` (`spec_addr(&result) == self@.start`). `T` is
214.             // a bare `Address` (no `View` bound), so the value is projected
215.             // through the universal `spec_addr`, not `result@`. `Address: Copy`,
216.             // so the field read is identity (`result == self.start`), which
217.             // discharges the postcondition by congruence of `spec_addr`.
218.             crate::hal::mem::spec_addr(&result) == self@.start,
219.     )]
220.     pub fn start(&self) -> T {
221.         // VERUS REWRITE: original exec body was `self.start.clone()`.
222.         // Verus limitation: `Clone::clone` on a generic `T: Address` has no spec
223.         // relating `spec_addr(&result)` to `spec_addr(&self.start)`, so the
224.         // postcondition `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` cannot be discharged
225.         // through `.clone()`. Minimal reproducer — restoring `self.start.clone()`:
226.         //   error: postcondition not satisfied
227.         //     --> region.rs:218:13  (spec_addr(&result) == self@.start)
228.         //     221 | self.start.clone()  -- at the end of the function body
229.         //   verification results:: 40 verified, 1 errors
230.         // `Address: Copy` (sys/mm/address/mod.rs:33) makes the direct field read
231.         // identity (`result == self.start`), discharging the postcondition.
232.         // Semantically equivalent: clone of a `Copy` type is a bitwise copy.
233.         self.start
234.     }
235. 
236.     /// Returns the size of the target memory region.
237.     #[verus_spec(result =>
238.         ensures
239.             result as int == self@.size,
240.     )]
241.     pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
242.         self.size
243.     }
244. 
245.     /// Returns the type of the target memory region.
246.     pub fn typ(&self) -> MemoryRegionType {
247.         self.typ
248.     }
249. 
250.     /// Returns the permissions of the target memory region.
251.     pub fn perm(&self) -> AccessPermission {
252.         self.perm
253.     }

256.     /// # Description

258.     /// Returns the MMIO cache policy of the target memory region, if set.
259.     ///

261.     ///
262.     /// The [`MmioCachePolicy`] if one was assigned, or `None` otherwise.
263.     ///
264.     pub fn cache_policy(&self) -> Option<MmioCachePolicy> {
265.         self.cache_policy

269.     /// # Description
270.     ///
271.     /// Sets the MMIO cache policy of the target memory region.
272.     ///
273.     /// # Parameters
274.     ///
275.     /// - `policy`: The cache policy to assign.
276.     ///

311. ///
312. /// # Description
313. ///
314. /// A memory region that has been truncated to a multiple of a page size.
315. ///
316. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
317. #[derive(Clone)]
318. pub struct TruncatedMemoryRegion<T: Address>(MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>);
319. 
320. impl<T: Address> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
321.     /// Creates a new truncated memory region.
322.     pub fn new(
323.         name: &str,
324.         start: PageAligned<T>,
325.         size: usize,
326.         typ: MemoryRegionType,
327.         perm: AccessPermission,
328.     ) -> Result<Self, Error> {
329.         // Truncate the size of the memory region to a multiple of the page size.
330.         let size: usize = ::sys::mm::align_up(size, PAGE_ALIGNMENT).ok_or_else(|| {
331.             let reason: &str = "align_up overflow";
332.             error!("TruncatedMemoryRegion::new(): {reason} (name={name:?}, size={size})");
333.             Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason)
334.         })?;
335.         Ok(Self(MemoryRegion::new(name, start, size, typ, perm)?))
336.     }
337. 
338.     ///
339.     /// # Description
340.     ///
341.     /// Creates a new truncated MMIO memory region with an explicit cache policy.
342.     ///
343.     /// # Parameters
344.     ///
345.     /// - `name`: Name of the memory region.
346.     /// - `start`: Page-aligned start address.
347.     /// - `size`: Size of the region in bytes (rounded up to page alignment).
348.     /// - `perm`: Access permissions for the region.
349.     /// - `cache_policy`: Caching policy that controls PWT/PCD bits in page table entries.
350.     ///
351.     /// # Returns
352.     ///
353.     /// Upon successful completion, a new [`TruncatedMemoryRegion`] with type
354.     /// [`MemoryRegionType::Mmio`] is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
355.     ///
356.     pub fn new_mmio(
357.         name: &str,
358.         start: PageAligned<T>,
359.         size: usize,
360.         perm: AccessPermission,
361.         cache_policy: MmioCachePolicy,
362.     ) -> Result<Self, Error> {
363.         let mut region: Self = Self::new(name, start, size, MemoryRegionType::Mmio, perm)?;
364.         region.0.set_cache_policy(cache_policy);
365.         Ok(region)

 ## Trait Obligations
 
 The target functions implement no trait; they are inherent accessors. However the values
 they expose feed `Ord`/`PartialOrd` for both region types, which sort **by start address**
 (`self.start.cmp(&other.start)` / delegated). Callers that keep regions in ordered/overlap
 structures (mmio allocator, kernel_vas lists) therefore rely on `start` being the stable
 ordering key.
 
 ---
 
 ## Caller Expectations
 
 ### `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start`
 - **Callers assume:** returns the region's first valid address as a `PageAligned<T>`, i.e.
   the value is page-aligned by construction (callers feed it straight into
   `into_frame_number`, `into_inner`, `into_raw_value` and treat it as a frame/page base
   with no re-alignment). The address equals the `start` passed at construction.
 - **Callers assume (range math):** `start.into_raw_value() + (size - 1)` does not overflow
   for valid regions — guaranteed because `MemoryRegion::new` rejected regions whose end
   exceeds `T::max_addr()`.
 - **Callers don't care about:** the `name`, `typ`, `perm`, `cache_policy` fields, nor that
   the value is stored inside a wrapped `MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>`. The return is purely
   the start address.
 
 ### `MemoryRegion::start`
 - **Callers assume:** returns the start address `T` exactly as supplied at construction (a
   faithful clone), suitable for `from_virtual_address` conversion and `align_down`.
 - **Callers don't care about:** alignment guarantees (unlike the truncated variant, this `T`
   is *not* necessarily page-aligned — `from_memory_region` explicitly `align_down`s it).
 
 ### `TruncatedMemoryRegion::size`
 - **Callers assume:** returns the byte length, which is a **non-zero multiple of the page
   size** (`size % page_size == 0`, `size >= 1`). Frame-count callers depend on exact
   divisibility: `size / FRAME_SIZE` is used without remainder handling, and `size - 1` is
   used as an inclusive-end offset assuming `size >= 1`. The page-multiple property comes
   from `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new` (`align_up(size, PAGE_ALIGNMENT)`) and is captured by
   the existing `inv()` (`self@.size % spec_page_size() == 0`).
 - **Callers don't care about:** how truncation happened or any other field.
 
 ### `MemoryRegion::size`
 - **Callers (internal only) assume:** returns the byte length as supplied/validated by
   `new` (`size >= 1`, end within the address space). It is forwarded verbatim into the
   truncated constructor, so no alignment is assumed at this layer.
 - **Callers don't care about:** alignment — the multiple-of-page property is established
   later by `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`, not here.
 
 ### Cross-cutting consistency expectation
 Across all four, callers rely on the pair `(start, size)` describing a half-open byte
 interval `[start, start + size)` that lies entirely within the address space and does not
 wrap, so derived values — inclusive end `start + size - 1`, frame range
 `[start/FRAME_SIZE, (start+size)/FRAME_SIZE)`, overlap tests — are well-defined.
 
 ---
 
 ## Abstract Resource
 
 This module models an **address-space interval with metadata**: a contiguous byte range
 identified by a start address and a size, tagged with type/permissions/cache policy.
 `TruncatedMemoryRegion` is the same interval constrained so that both endpoints are
 page-aligned (start is `PageAligned<T>`, size is a page-size multiple), making it directly
 usable for paging/frame booking. From the caller's perspective the only state that matters
 for the target accessors is the `(start, size)` geometry; the View should expose `start`
 and `size` as abstract integers (already present as `MemoryRegionView.start: int` /
 `size: int`).
 
 ---
 
 ## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
 
 - `start` and `size` are immutable for a region's lifetime; the accessors are pure and
   return values equal to the constructor inputs (modulo truncation for the truncated
   variant). Repeated calls return the same value.
 - `size >= 1` for every constructed region (`new` rejects `size == 0`).
 - The interval does not overflow the address space: `start + size - 1 <= T::max_addr()`.
 - For `TruncatedMemoryRegion`: `start` is page-aligned and `size % page_size == 0`
   (existing `inv()`), so `size / FRAME_SIZE` is exact and `start` needs no re-alignment.
 - `start` is the ordering key (`Ord`); equal-start regions compare equal on start.
 
 ---
 
 ## Pre-existing Specs (from upstream verification)
 
 - **Source:** `region.spec.rs` is an empty `verus! { }` stub — no executable specs.
 - **Functions with specs:** none (`grep verus_spec region.rs` → none).
 - **View type:** **exists** in the in-file `verus!` block — `MemoryRegionView { start: int,
   size: int, typ, perm, cache_policy }`, with `View` impls for both `MemoryRegion<T>` and
   `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` (the latter forwards to the inner region), plus
   `TruncatedMemoryRegion::inv()` requiring page-aligned `start`/`size`.
 
 ### Assessment
 - **Coverage:** partial — a View and `inv()` exist, but none of the four target accessors
   have `ensures` linking their return value to `self@.start` / `self@.size`.
 - **Strength:** weak for the accessors — callers above need `start() == self@.start` and
   `size() == self@.size` (as the abstract int) to discharge range/frame arithmetic; these
   ensures are currently missing.
 - **View design:** caller-abstract and adequate — `start`/`size` as `int` exactly match what
   every caller uses (`into_raw_value`, frame math, overlap tests). No field is biased toward
   a single caller. The `closed` view is fine; accessor `ensures` should bridge to it.

1. # View Design: hal::mem::types::region
2. 
3. Status: **review & refinement** of the View already present in the in-file
4. `verus! { }` block of `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/region.rs`. The existing
5. `MemoryRegionView` is sound and caller-abstract; this document confirms each
6. field against the substitution test, proposes a strengthened `inv()`, and
7. records the spec transition and reusable spec helpers that later phases will
8. reference.
9. 
10. In-scope verification-order targets:
11. `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start`, `MemoryRegion::start`,
12. `TruncatedMemoryRegion::size`, `MemoryRegion::size`. The View, however, is
13. module-level: it is the shared abstraction for *both* region types and all of
14. their accessors, not just the four targets.
15. 
16. ---
17. 
18. ## Abstract Resource
19. 
20. A **memory region** is a contiguous, non-wrapping half-open byte interval of the
21. address space, `[start, start + size)`, tagged with metadata
22. (type / permissions / cache policy). `TruncatedMemoryRegion` is the same
23. interval additionally constrained so both endpoints are page-aligned (`start`
24. page-aligned, `size` a multiple of the page size), making it directly usable for
25. frame/page booking.
26. 
27. From the caller's perspective the only state that matters is the **geometry**
28. `(start, size)` plus the three **metadata tags** that other accessors expose.
29. Everything else (the human-readable `name`, the wrapping of one struct inside
30. another for the truncated variant, the physical layout of the fields) is
31. internal.
32. 
33. ---
34. 
35. ## View Struct
36. 
37. Both `MemoryRegion<T>` and `TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` map to the **same** View
38. type. The truncated wrapper forwards `view()` to its inner region, so a single
39. abstraction describes both. `T: Address + View<V = int>`, hence addresses are
40. abstracted to `int`.
41. 
42. ```rust
43. pub struct MemoryRegionView {
44.     /// First valid byte address of the region (abstract address, in bytes).
45.     /// Equals the `start` supplied at construction; for the truncated variant
46.     /// it is page-aligned. This is also the Ord key for both region types.
47.     pub start: int,
48.     /// Length of the region in bytes. The interval is [start, start + size).
49.     /// For the truncated variant it is a multiple of the page size.
50.     pub size: int,
51.     /// Classification of the region (Usable / Reserved / Mmio / Bad).
52.     pub typ: MemoryRegionType,
53.     /// Access permissions granted over the region.
54.     pub perm: AccessPermission,
55.     /// Optional MMIO caching policy (PWT/PCD); `None` for non-MMIO regions.
56.     pub cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>,
57. }
58. ```
59. 
60. `view()` stays `closed` on both impls (callers reference `self@.start` etc. but
61. the field-to-storage mapping does not leak). The impls are **unconditional**
62. over `T: Address` and project the typed `start` through the universal
63. `spec_addr<T: Address>` ghost function (defined in `page.spec.rs`), exactly as
64. `PageAligned<T>` does — **not** via a `T: View<V = int>` bound and `self.start@`:
65. 
66. ```rust
67. impl<T: Address> View for MemoryRegion<T> {
68.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
69.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView {
70.         MemoryRegionView { start: spec_addr(&self.start), size: self.size as int, .. }
71.     }
72. }
73. 
74. impl<T: Address> View for TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
75.     type V = MemoryRegionView;
76.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> MemoryRegionView { self.0@ }   // forward
77. }
78. ```
79. 
80. > **Design change (implemented).** The originally-proposed
81. > `impl<T: Address + View<V = int>>` bound is **not usable**: the in-scope exec
82. > accessors live in `impl<T: Address> ...` blocks (no `View` bound), so a
83. > conditional `View` impl makes `self@` untypable inside them
84. > (`error[E0599]: MemoryRegion<T>: View not satisfied`). Moreover the
85. > address-family `View` impls are all `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated, so a
86. > `T: View<V = int>` bound would be unsatisfiable in a normal `cargo build`.
87. > The fix mirrors the established `PageAligned<T>` pattern: make `View`
88. > unconditional and project addresses through the universal `spec_addr`. This
89. > keeps the `view()` closed and the abstraction `T`-agnostic while letting every
90. > accessor contract typecheck for a bare `T: Address`.
91. 
92. ---
93. 
94. ## Well-formedness Invariant
95. 
96. The current in-file `inv()` (defined only on `TruncatedMemoryRegion`) captures
97. **only** page alignment:
98. 
99. ```rust
100. &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0
101. &&& self@.size  % spec_page_size() == 0
102. ```
103. 
104. The caller analysis shows two further geometry properties that every constructed
105. region guarantees and that callers *depend on* for their arithmetic
106. (`size - 1`, `start + size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`). These should be made part
107. of the abstract well-formedness so they are available wherever a region is in
108. scope. Recommended layering:
109. 
110. ```rust
111. // Shared geometry well-formedness, valid for BOTH region types.
112. // (Proposed as a reusable helper on the View — see "Spec Helpers" below.)
113. //   non-empty:  size >= 1                (new rejects size == 0)
114. //   no-wrap:    start >= 0 && start + size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
115. //               (the interval fits the address space; start + size - 1 never
116. //                overflows, so inclusive-end / frame-range math is well-defined)
117. 
118. impl<T: Address + View<V = int>> MemoryRegion<T> {
119.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
120.         self@.wf_geometry()
121.     }
122. }
123. 
124. impl<T: Address + View<V = int>> TruncatedMemoryRegion<T> {
125.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
126.         &&& self@.wf_geometry()                       // size >= 1, no wrap
127.         &&& self@.start % spec_page_size() == 0       // page-aligned start
128.         &&& self@.size  % spec_page_size() == 0       // page-multiple size
129.     }
130. }
131. ```
132. 
133. Notes:
134. - The no-wrap bound is stated abstractly against `usize::MAX` (the widest
135.   address representation). The concrete `T::max_addr()` bound enforced by `new`
136.   is *stronger*; the View only needs the weaker no-wrap fact because that is all
137.   caller arithmetic relies on, and it keeps the invariant `T`-agnostic.
138. - **Implemented as designed.** Both `MemoryRegion::inv` (`wf_geometry()`) and the
139.   strengthened `TruncatedMemoryRegion::inv` (`wf_geometry()` + page alignment) are
140.   in `region.spec.rs`. Adding `wf_geometry` caused no proof churn: `inv()` is an
141.   `open spec fn` referenced by no in-scope contract, so it imposes no obligation
142.   on the four accessors (it documents the abstract well-formedness for callers
143.   and future phases). `wf_geometry`, `spec_end`, `spec_last`, `contains`, and the
144.   `spec_set_cache_policy` transition are all present as View helpers.
145. 
146. ---
147. 
148. ## Spec Helpers (on the View type)
149. 
150. Per the skill, reusable spec logic lives on the View, not as extra `pub spec
151. fn`s on the region impls. These encode exactly the derived quantities callers
152. compute, so later `ensures` can hand them back directly.
153. 
154. ```rust
155. impl MemoryRegionView {
156.     /// Non-empty, non-wrapping interval within the address space.
157.     pub open spec fn wf_geometry(self) -> bool {
158.         &&& self.size >= 1
159.         &&& self.start >= 0
160.         &&& self.start + self.size <= usize::MAX as int + 1
161.     }
162. 
163.     /// Exclusive end of the half-open interval [start, end).
164.     pub open spec fn spec_end(self) -> int { self.start + self.size }
165. 
166.     /// Inclusive last byte address (callers compute `start + size - 1`).
167.     pub open spec fn spec_last(self) -> int { self.start + self.size - 1 }
168. 
169.     /// Whether `addr` lies in [start, start + size).
170.     pub open spec fn contains(self, addr: int) -> bool {
171.         self.start <= addr < self.start + self.size
172.     }
173. }
174. ```
175. 
176. These are optional conveniences for downstream phases; the four target
177. accessors themselves only need `result@ == self@.start` / `result == self@.size`
178. style `ensures`. They are listed so spec authors reuse one definition of
179. "inclusive end" / "contains" instead of re-deriving overflow-prone arithmetic.
180. 
181. ---
182. 
183. ## Spec Transition Functions
184. 
185. The region types are almost entirely immutable. The **only** state-mutating
186. exec function in the module is `MemoryRegion::set_cache_policy`, so it gets the
187. sole transition (it is out of the current four-function scope but belongs to the
188. View design for completeness):
189. 
190. ```rust
191. impl MemoryRegionView {
192.     pub open spec fn spec_set_cache_policy(self, policy: MmioCachePolicy) -> MemoryRegionView {
193.         MemoryRegionView { cache_policy: Some(policy), ..self }   // frame: geometry + tags preserved
194.     }
195. }
196. // ensures self@ == old(self)@.spec_set_cache_policy(policy)
197. ```
198. 
199. `..self` is the frame condition: `start`, `size`, `typ`, `perm` are unchanged.
200. 
201. The constructors (`MemoryRegion::new`, `TruncatedMemoryRegion::new`,
202. `new_mmio`, `from_memory_region`, `from_virtual_memory_region`) are *creation*,
203. not `self`-transitions; they will be specified in later phases by stating the
204. resulting `self@` (e.g. `result@.start == start@`, `result@.size` rounded up to
205. a page multiple for the truncated path) rather than via a transition on an
206. existing View. No transition function is owed for them here.
207. 
208. The four in-scope accessors are pure reads — no transition, just `ensures`
209. linking the return value to the View field. Because the return types (`T`,
210. `PageAligned<T>`) are bare `Address` values (no `View` bound in the exec impl),
211. the returned address is projected through `spec_addr`, not `result@`:
212. 
213. | Function | Implemented ensures |
214. |----------|----------------------------|
215. | `MemoryRegion::start`            | `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` |
216. | `MemoryRegion::size`             | `result as int == self@.size`   |
217. | `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start`   | `spec_addr(&result) == self@.start` (page alignment of `self@.start` follows from `self.inv()`) |
218. | `TruncatedMemoryRegion::size`    | `result as int == self@.size`   |
219. 
220. `TruncatedMemoryRegion::start` delegates to `MemoryRegion::start`; the forwarding
221. `view()` (`self@ == self.0@`) makes `spec_addr(&result) == self.0@.start ==
222. self@.start` discharge by delegation. `MemoryRegion::start` itself carries a
223. specification-phase `admit()` placeholder: relating `spec_addr(&self.start.clone())`
224. to `spec_addr(&self.start)` needs a value-preserving clone spec on the `Address`
225. family, which is supplied in the proving phase.
226. 
227. ---
228. 
229. ## Design Rationale (per field, substitution test)
230. 
231. > Substitution test: *if the implementation were completely rewritten with a
232. > different algorithm, would this field still make sense?*
233. 
234. | Field | Caller-observable via | Substitution test | Verdict |
235. |-------|-----------------------|--------------------|---------|
236. | `start: int` | `start()` (10 ext. sites: frame number, raw value, identity-map base, overlap key, Ord key) | Any region representation must expose a first address; callers read it as a frame/page base and as the ordering key. Independent of how it is stored (`T` vs `PageAligned<T>`). | ✅ keep |
237. | `size: int` | `size()` (8 ext. sites: `size - 1`, `size / FRAME_SIZE`, region end, identity-map end) | Any representation must expose a byte length; callers do exact frame division and inclusive-end math. Survives any storage/truncation strategy. | ✅ keep |
238. | `typ: MemoryRegionType` | `typ()` (14 refs) — routing/classification of regions | The classification is intrinsic region state, not an implementation artifact; survives a rewrite. Needed so `typ()` can later be specified. | ✅ keep |
239. | `perm: AccessPermission` | `perm()` — permissions consumed when mapping | Intrinsic region attribute, independent of layout. | ✅ keep |
240. | `cache_policy: Option<MmioCachePolicy>` | `cache_policy()` / mutated by `set_cache_policy()` | Intrinsic MMIO attribute and the target of the module's only mutator; the transition spec needs it. | ✅ keep |
241. 
242. Abstract-type choices: `int` for `start`/`size` (not `usize`/`T`) so spec
243. arithmetic — inclusive end, frame ranges, overlap — is overflow-free and matches
244. how every caller uses the values (`into_raw_value()` then integer math). `Option`
245. mirrors the optional cache policy. `typ`/`perm` are small `Copy` enums/structs
246. carried as-is; abstracting them further would add no caller value.
247. 
248. Shared View for both region types: the truncated variant *is* the same interval
249. with a stronger invariant, and its `view()` forwards to the inner region. One
250. View + a stronger `inv()` is simpler than two near-identical View types and lets
251. callers (e.g. `MmioRegion::base`/`size`, the mmio allocator) reason uniformly.
252. 
253. `view()` closed / `inv()` open: `closed` hides the field→storage mapping (e.g.
254. that truncated regions wrap `MemoryRegion<PageAligned<T>>`); `open` `inv()`
255. exposes the page-alignment and geometry facts callers must rely on
256. (`size / FRAME_SIZE` exact, `start` needs no re-alignment).
257. 
258. ---
259. 
260. ## Rejected Alternatives
261. 
262. - **`name: String` field** — `name()` is a public accessor, but the caller
263.   analysis explicitly states callers "don't care about" the name for any
264.   geometry/booking use, and no in-scope spec references it. Including it fails
265.   *minimality* (no spec uses it) without aiding any caller. It is display /
266.   identity metadata; if `name()` is ever brought into scope, add a
267.   `name: Seq<char>` field then. **Excluded.**
268. 
269. - **`start: T` / `start: PageAligned<T>` (machine/typed address)** — mirrors the
270.   implementation field and forces callers to unwrap before doing arithmetic.
271.   Fails the abstract-type rule. The `int` abstraction (via `T::view() == int`)
272.   is what every caller actually computes on. **Excluded.**
273. 
274. - **`size: usize` / `nat`** — `usize` re-introduces overflow into specs;
275.   `nat` would block expressing the no-wrap bound against `usize::MAX as int`
276.   cleanly and complicates `size - 1` reasoning. `int` is the right spec type.
277.   **Excluded.**
278. 
279. - **`end: int` as a stored field (instead of `size`)** — redundant with
280.   `start + size`; storing both invites an extra consistency clause in `inv()`.
281.   Callers want *both* numbers, but only one is primitive state — `end` is a
282.   derived helper (`spec_end`), not a field. **Excluded as a field; kept as a
